reason: The front of the arm has an empty biceps slot, and the chapter says to build it using muscle cells.
expectation: The muscle cells will help form the biceps at the front of the arm.

effect: The muscle cells formed the biceps, but the radius still needs mineral.
reaction: The picture made the biceps pulling to bend the elbow clear.
reason: The front arm's bone is still awaiting mineral, which the chapter says hardens the attachment.
expectation: The mineral will strengthen the bone where the biceps tendon pulls.

effect: The mineral strengthened the radius, completing the front-arm goal.
reaction: It is clear that the mineral hardens bone without hardening the tendon.
reason: The back of the arm needs a triceps, and the chapter says to build it from the same kind of muscle cells.
expectation: The muscle cells will form the triceps at the back of the arm.

effect: The muscle cells formed the triceps, but the ulna still needs mineral.
reaction: It is interesting that the muscle's position makes its pull straighten the elbow instead of bending it.
reason: The back-arm goal also requires strengthening the bone attachment, and the ulna is still awaiting mineral.
expectation: The mineral will strengthen the ulna where the triceps tendon pulls.

effect: Mineral strengthened the ulna without hardening the tendons or joint surfaces, completing the back-arm goal.
reaction: The contrast between hard bone and soft connecting tissues was clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the triceps was most worthwhile because its position behind the elbow explained how a pull can straighten the arm, unlike the biceps pull in front.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding mineral to the second bone felt repetitive after seeing the same idea at the front, though it completed the other attachment.

surprise.text: The same kind of muscle cells could have different effects because of where the muscles attach and pull.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary: the muscle and mineral pairings were named in the goals and pictures.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see how other body parts work together; the comparison between bending and straightening made this chapter interesting, even though the mineral steps were repetitive.
